Design Decisions (179-185) states rationale for OQ-1 through OQ-4 and #134 OQ-3. No unjustified 'we will use X' statement found.

design.md carries no literally-named '## Open Questions' heading; the equivalent content is '## Design Decisions (Resolving Open Questions)' (179-185), which resolves all seven investigation.md open questions (#133 OQ1-4 at investigation.md:174-177, #134 OQ1-3 at investigation.md:181-183), each with a stated resolution and rationale, none left blocking. Under legacy_design: true (precheck-result.json) this heading-naming difference is a [LEGACY COMPAT] Minor advisory, not a Major gap, per reviewer-calibration.md:86-88.

investigation.md is present and grounds INV-001 through INV-017, so the 'investigation.md absent' Major does not apply. design.md itself introduces no separate ungrounded '## Assumptions' section (folded into Risks/Design Decisions instead). The requirements-level assumptions it builds on are each grounded: the SIGTERM-termination assumption is not merely deferred but exercised by a dedicated test (Edge Case 7 -> design.md item 2(b) / TEST-004(b)); the install.sh:758-781 convention citation's provenance gap is explicitly disclosed and independently supported by the first-hand command -v result (requirements.md:177); the 2-second SIGTERM grace is explicitly flagged as an accepted, challengeable guess (design.md:245, Risks section).

design.md has no '## Constraint Compliance' section, so the TYPE-H fallback scan applies. Nearly all requirements.md constraints (BL-001, BL-002, BL-003, BL-005, REQ-003's 'must not exit 2', Edge Case 1's 'must not depend on GNU coreutils', Edge Case 6's must-not-false-report) are addressed. One is directly contradicted: design.md:224 ('6. BL-004 -- parity. Every case above exists in both tests/cross-model.tests.sh and .ps1.') is stated with no runtime carve-out, so it reads as requiring AC-004's sub-case (b) in both suites. That contradicts requirements.md's own BL-004/AC-004 text: the runtime table at requirements.md:57-60 and the explicit statement at requirements.md:67 ('the PowerShell suite carries no (b) sub-case -- writing one would be a test that cannot fail'), reinforced at requirements.md:75 ('BL-004's parity requirement is satisfied at the level of outcome... not by mirroring a POSIX signal model onto a platform that has no equivalent') and acceptance-tests.md's TEST-004 table at :64-68 ('(b) escalation is reached | ... | none, deliberately'). This is the identical contradiction class requirements.md:62 records round 3 of spec review catching and fixing in an earlier draft. design.md's own Test Strategy item 2 (212-220) and the Coverage table row for AC-004 (design.md:200) never restate the PowerShell exemption either, so nothing in design.md disambiguates line 224's 'every case' language. A task author implementing literally from design.md's Test Strategy could write a PowerShell (b) test case that cannot fail -- the exact vacuous-test defect this specification fought three rounds to eliminate. Concrete fix: line 224 needs the same runtime carve-out requirements.md and acceptance-tests.md already state.

requirements.md's REQ-002/AC-004 impose a concrete wall-clock bound (SDD_PANELIST_TIMEOUT, default 600s) on an external call -- this feature's latency/SLA-shaped constraint. design.md addresses it directly: the bounded-wait helper (API & Contract Plan, 33-106) is the mechanism, and Test Strategy item 2 / TEST-004 verifies it with explicit timing assertions (elapsed wall-clock within a 10s margin, boundary-race sub-case repeated at least 5 iterations). infra-spec.md:15 additionally notes the CI timing cost (~3s/case across a 3-OS matrix) is deliberately kept small to avoid flakiness.

design.md's '## Deployment & CI Plan' (228-232) states no new CI step, names the existing test job and tests/run-all.sh, and the waivable stack descriptor. infra-spec.md (required layer doc, in this round's manifest) supplies deployment target (scripts run on the operator's machine via the cross-model-verify skill; docs are repository-only, per infra-spec.md:19-28), CI/CD sequence, and a Rollback section (infra-spec.md:30-38) including the explicit note that reverting Stream A alone reopens the DoS hole. Data Plan states 'No data changes' (design.md:151), so migration-execution-order is inapplicable. No feature-flag strategy is stated, but none is required: the change is additive behind an env var with a safe default and is not a phased/incremental UI rollout.

design.md's '## Data Plan' states 'No data changes. This feature introduces no database, no persisted schema, and no new document format.' (design.md:151), which is this check's explicit auto-pass condition.

The one external integration this feature touches -- the vendor panelist CLIs (codex, gemini) -- is identified with purpose and trust posture (Security Boundaries B1, design.md:168), its concrete invocation contract (call-site code, design.md:71-74 and 93-96), and exhaustively tabulated failure behaviour (Failure Taxonomy table, design.md:124-131, cross-checked by the STRIDE table in security-spec.md:29-37). The deliberate non-pinning of CLI version/behaviour is a stated, rationale-backed limitation (Non-goals, requirements.md:162; OQ-1, design.md:181), not a silent gap, satisfying the calibration rule that a defer-with-rationale is not a finding.

The Components table (design.md:17-27) lists exactly the artifacts REQ-001..006 require (4 runner scripts, the policy doc, the threat-model doc, 2 test suites) plus one explicitly-untouched file (check-cross-model.sh, per BL-002) -- no extra component. The REQ-to-AC roll-up (design.md:193) and the AC-to-TEST coverage table (195-210) show 1:1 coverage of all 14 ACs with no addition or omission (the table's own stated purpose, design.md:191, is exactly to catch this class of defect after attempt 1's two BLOCKED rounds). requirements.md carries no '## Goals'/'## User Stories' headings (an issue-driven REQ/AC document instead); every REQ-001..006 is reachable through the roll-up table with no requirement left uncovered by any component.

High-risk surfaces are present (B1 process-kill/DoS-fix, B2 truncated-verdict spoofing, B4 hook-trust bypass) and each names a concrete acceptance-test artifact rather than requiring live execution: B1 -> TEST-004 (security-spec.md:57-58), B2 -> TEST-005/TEST-006 (security-spec.md:59-60), B4 -> TEST-010 (security-spec.md:63). The Boundary-to-Test table in security-spec.md (55-63) and the AC/TEST coverage table in design.md (195-210) together give every high-risk claim a named, inspectable verification artifact.
